newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Empire hurt by property woes hits year-low.
newsitem.headline: Empire hurt by property woes hits year-low.

text.p: Empire East Land Holdings Inc dipped to its year-low level, shedding 60 centavos, or 10.34 percent, to 5.20 pesos in late trade on Friday on fears of an oversupply in the property sector, brokers said.

"There's still the overhang on the property sector, that there's a glut especially on the high end and loan problems for the low end," said Michael Julian, dealer at Philippine Asia Equity Securities.
Empire's parent firm, Megaworld Properties & Holdings Inc, also plunged 70 centavos, or 11.67 percent, to its year-low at 5.30 pesos.
"The property sector is still consolidating. The market is probably not yet convinced of Megaworld's denials," said Henry Ong, analyst at Sapphire Securities.
Both Megaworld and Empire have denied rumours they were cash-strapped.
Empire East's share price in late trade was way below its offer price last year of 12.90 pesos. Trading in Empire was heavier at 6.62 million shares than Megaworld's 1.70 million shares.
